missingCandidates.proposition: Mark and Luke give materially different portrayals of Jesus's conduct and outlook at death, and combining their sayings produces a harmonized account found in none of the Gospels.
missingCandidates.rationale: This is Ehrman's principal extended sayings-and-deeds example, distinct from the selected detail-change challenge and carrying his explicit argument that harmonization replaces rather than preserves each Gospel's portrayal.

missingCandidates.proposition: Multiple historically tested activities—including Jesus's baptism, preaching, healing, disciples, temple controversy, crucifixion, and the continued movement—form an essential and sufficient core from which the principal contours of his public life can be known.
missingCandidates.rationale: This is Evans's direct constructive answer on the historical activities of Jesus, supported with explicit historical criteria and examples; no selected move otherwise preserves this major case.

conclusion: All 26 selected moves have correct attribution, supported propositions, sufficient cited spans, source-exact eligible quotations, and valid response targets. The inventory is nevertheless incomplete because it omits the central Mark-versus-Luke passion comparison and Evans's corresponding historically supported core of Jesus's activities.
